title: Map: Track the spread of measles in the U.S.
snippet:
Measles, one of the most contagious viruses in the world, is regularly infecting people in the U.S. again.

Already in 2026 more than 2,300 cases have been counted, making 2026 the two year for measles infections in the U.S. since 2000.

NBC News is continuing to track confirmed measles cases across the United States, using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

Measles case counts reached a 34-year high last year, and seven months into 2026, this year’s total is even higher. [...] CORRECTION (Feb. 20, 2026, 3:57 p.m. ET): A previous version of a graphic in this article miscalculated the relative size of this year's measles case count. As of Feb. 20, this year's case count is four times the size of 2025's at the same point in the year, and 25 times the size of 2024's at the same point, not seven times and 30 times higher.

Add NBC News to Google

Joe Murphy

Joe Murphy is a data editor at NBC News.

Melinda Yao

I am an intern for NBC News’ Data / Graphics team. [...] The major outbreaks last year began with West Texas in February. In October, a measles outbreak occurred along the Utah and Arizona border. In all, the CDC recorded 48 measles outbreaks in 2025, up from 16 in 2024. So far in 2026, 35 measles outbreaks have been reported.

Childhood vaccination rates have been backsliding, leaving communities vulnerable to this deadly disease.

title: Measles cases in 2026 are set to surpass last year's total. Here's why - ABC News
snippet:
In the decade before the measles vaccine became available, the CDC estimates that 3 to 4 million in the U.S. were sickened by measles every year, about 48,000 were hospitalized and about 400 to 500 people died. About 1,000 people suffer encephalitis every year. [...] Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shows the U.S. has reported 2,231 cases as of July 9, which is just 58 shy of the 2,289 cases reported for the entirety of 2025.

Previously, the 2025 total was the highest number of cases seen in more than 30 years, and some public health specialists believe the U.S. is on track to lose the elimination status it earned in 2000. [...] ## Live

title: Shapiro Administration Launches Measles Dashboard | Department of Health | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
snippet:
# Shapiro Administration Launches Measles Dashboard to Keep Parents, Public Informed of Ongoing Cases and Highlights Work to Triple Vaccinations in Lancaster County

The Department of Health launches measles dashboard to keep Pennsylvanians better informed about cases and ongoing efforts to contain the spread among people who are unvaccinated.

In Lancaster County, state health center staff more than tripled the number of measles vaccines administered in 2026 thus far, compared to 2025. [...] Two doses of the MMR vaccine is the best protection against the measles virus, as it is 97% effective at preventing a person from ever contracting it. The vaccine has long-proven effectiveness over several decades. Since the vaccine was introduced in the early 1960s, cases and deaths from measles in the U.S. decreased more than 97% compared to the pre-vaccine era. [...] The new dashboard will be updated Monday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons with the latest data available. In addition to the number of cases per county, the dashboard includes demographic data, hospitalization rate, and vaccination status of the cases.

title: CDC adds almost 100 new cases to expanding US measles outbreak
snippet:
All but 16 of this year’s cases have been locally acquired, with the rest tied to international travel.

The CDC noted 38 outbreaks, one more than last week. Last year saw 48 measles outbreaks, defined as three or more related cases.

Of the 2026 cases, 20% involve children age 5 and under, and 68% involve kids and young adults to age 19. Seven percent of patients have been hospitalized, compared with 11% in 2025. Among all measles patients, 93% are unvaccinated or have unknown vaccine status. [...] Arizona recorded two new cases") this week, 121 total. Many of the newest cases are in Maricopa County.

In promising news, Virginia") reported no new cases for the fourth straight week. It had previously been a measles hot spot. Its total remains at 177.

title: Measles
snippet:
Before the introduction of measles vaccine in 1963 and widespread vaccination, major epidemics occurred approximately every two to three years and caused an estimated 2.6 million deaths each year.

An estimated 95 000 people died from measles in 2024 – mostly children under the age of five years, despite the availability of a safe and cost-effective vaccine. [...] WHO continues to strengthen the Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network (GMRLN) to ensure timely diagnosis of measles and track the virus’ spread to assist countries in coordinating targeted vaccination activities and reduce deaths from this vaccine-preventable disease.

### The IA2030 Measles & Rubella Partnership [...] Accelerated immunization activities by countries, WHO, the Measles & Rubella Partnership, and other international partners successfully prevented an estimated 59 million deaths between 2000 and 2024. Vaccination decreased an estimated measles deaths from 780 000 in 2000 to 95 000 in 2024 (1).
